stories.title: Anthropic's IPO meets the AI backlash: investors now expect $1 trillion to $1.5 trillion
stories.summary: Anthropic, likely heading for a Nasdaq debut in mid-November, is seen by its investors at a $1 trillion to $1.5 trillion valuation, down from a $2 trillion target floated earlier, CNBC reports. US voters opposed data-centre ballot measures in 40 of 41 cases this week.

predictions.note: Local communities opposed data-centre ballot measures in 40 of 41 cases in the US midterms, CNBC reports.
More than half of voters told NBC's exit poll AI data centres were a crucial or major factor in their congressional vote.

stories.title: Meta's Muse scores 47% on Meta's own Personal Superintelligence Index, up from 38%
stories.summary: Meta is rolling out models trained with its Muse Wonder model to Muse and Meta AI. On Meta's own tests, Muse now scores 47% on its Personal Superintelligence Index (38% before) and uses critical context in 90% of tasks (76% before).

stories.title: Nous Research strips most Chinese state propaganda from Alibaba's Qwen model
stories.summary: Nous Research fine-tuned Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B on about 53 million tokens into Arete-27B. On Nous's own 803-prompt test, the share of answers containing propaganda fell from 22% to 0.9%.

stories.title: Tel Aviv University and Stanford get two AI models to teach each other without human data
stories.summary: In a preprint, one model generates symbol sequences and the other learns to predict them, with no human-made data; the skills transferred to language, images, audio, music, code and DNA. The models could not learn real-world facts this way.

stories.title: OpenAI closes $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, less than it hoped
stories.summary: OpenAI has closed $11 billion, the first part of a round valuing it at $1.25 trillion, people familiar told Bloomberg and Reuters. It could rise to $20 billion; OpenAI had hoped for up to $30 billion at $1.4 trillion.

predictions.note: OpenAI closed $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, a frontier lab priced at trillion-dollar scale.

stories.title: Goldman Sachs: the data-centre build-out could cost $8.5 trillion over five years
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs raised its 2030 forecast for global data-centre capacity to 273 GW from 217 GW, a build-out that could need $8.5 trillion of spending over five years, according to Investing.com's report of its note.

predictions.note: A projection: consensus capex for selected US tech and cloud firms could reach about $1.74 trillion a year by 2030, up from $457 billion in 2025.

stories.title: The US cleared Nvidia's H200 chips for a Chinese firm with an empty office
stories.summary: The Commerce Department approved dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia's H200 chips, The New York Times found, including New Matrix, a 17-month-old firm whose office is empty and whose owners have ties to a firm blacklisted since 2024.

predictions.note: US approvals let Nvidia's H200 chips go to a Chinese firm with an empty office and blacklist ties, a gap in tracking where AI chips go.

stories.title: One man runs 12 online brands with no employees, using AI as his team
stories.summary: Alex Willen expects his 12 e-commerce brands, which have no employees, to bring in $2.5 million to $3 million this year, CNBC reports. Non-employer business applications in AI-exposed industries rose 26.8% from early 2024 to early 2026, per preliminary Mercatus research.

stories.title: Cambridge's AI-designed bird flu vaccine fully protects animals in tests
stories.summary: A broad-spectrum bird flu vaccine designed with AI by the University of Cambridge and spinoff DIOSynVax gave complete protection against diverse variants in animal trials, while stockpiled vaccines protected about half of the animals. It has not been tested in people.

predictions.note: An AI-designed vaccine fully protected animals in a published study, a step well short of regulator approval.

stories.title: NYT Cooking's new AI assistant saves a reviewer's chicken, and nearly ruins her cake
stories.summary: The New York Times' cooking app has added an AI assistant for subscribers, on iOS at launch. In The Verge's hands-on review it helped with a weeknight chicken but almost ruined a cake.

stories.title: Elvis Presley's rightsholders and Eminem's publisher sue AI music maker Suno
stories.summary: A Presley group including Authentic Brands Group alleges Suno infringes copyright and Tennessee's ELVIS Act; Eight Mile Style, which controls hundreds of Eminem recordings, filed its own suit. 'The next Elvis won't pick up a guitar,' their lawyers wrote. Suno denies wrongdoing.

stories.title: Accused of using AI, the director of Dior's holiday film says it was drawn by hand
stories.summary: After a six-fingered hand went viral, director Sylvain Chomet and producer Aton Soumache told Variety the six-minute Dior film was traditional 2D animation that took seven months, with an automated tool filling in some in-between frames.

stories.title: A 78-year-old Philadelphia professor blocks Uber Eats delivery robots in protest
stories.summary: Semi-retired UPenn professor Carolyn Marvin stands in front of Uber Eats delivery robots, made by Avride, in downtown Philadelphia. Police handcuffed her and wrote her a ticket for disorderly conduct, which she plans to contest.

stories.title: Xinhua unveils two humanoid robot news anchors, their look designed by Zhang Yimou
stories.summary: China's state news agency Xinhua and UBTECH unveiled humanoid anchors Xinyu and Xinyan in Beijing on 5 November, linked to Xinhua's AI current-affairs agent. Film director Zhang Yimou was chief image designer; Xinhua says journalists remain the central editorial actors.

stories.title: Dubai gets the UAE's first humanoid robot showroom, with 28 robots
stories.summary: Lootah Robotics' showroom on Sheikh Zayed Road shows 28 robots priced from AED 50,000 to 3 million, for cleaning homes, facades, streets and warehouses, reception and hospitality. Dubai aims for 200,000 robots by 2032.

Goldman Sachs reckons the data centre boo m could cost $8.5 trillion in five years.

Wires dangling.

Stockpiled ones? About half.

But the future isn't just happening to us. We still get a say.
